P01.note: "the finest of the year in March and ... tedious in April" with "reversing themselves about as often" hands over mercurial; insistent and judicious die on the reversals.

P02.note: "the same number of checks per cart and the same share of warnings that became fines" gives evenhanded outright; "block by block" kills haphazard.

P03.note: "through a church charity that did not name its source" gives covert away; also the passage never says the ministry is national.

P04.note: Needs the petition-start and withdrawal-end sentences together, but each distractor is killed by a planted phrase ("two councils signed", "almost no cut weirs").

P05.note: "no day missing, and every page uses the same four columns" gives methodical away.

P06.note: "have become sounds without meaning" and "Several verses no longer make sense" give mangled away; the m- alliteration does not disguise it.

P07.note: Combines "only its finance committee" with "about five reached the full board"; distractors are weak, especially envoy.

P08.note: "built three new hospitals ... from the stone building's floor plan, staffed each with its number of nurses" is the definition of cloned; "went on as before" kills cannibalized.

P09.note: "sealed packet he never opened" and "corrected alone" kill confidant and critic; the carrying sentence gives courier.

P10.note: "could buy grain from no one else, and ... paid whatever price the house named" defines cornered.

P11.note: Needs "needed more time" over twenty years plus "without a single pencil mark"; the pencil-mark line kills updated and sanitized.

P12.note: Decline then revival must be combined, but the word "again" in "most households again kept a basket" gives rekindled away fairly cheaply.

P13.note: Slow lament versus twice the speed with foot-tapping; "kept every note" kills clipped.

P14.note: Keys in procession and painting behind the throne point to trophy; heavy garrison spending at a strait mouth keeps watchtower partly alive.

P15.note: Heard both sides, ruled either way, accepted as final; "went against the miner about as often as for him" kills megaphone.

P16.note: "left a ravine some twenty feet deep along the valley's full length" gives gouged away; "old riverbed lying dry" is a literal hook for emptied.

P17.note: "moves on to his grandfather's violin, the history of the county road, and a recipe for plum jam" gives digressive away.

P18.note: The spring-visits sentence gives ambassador; apprentice is a literal lure from "technician ... hired straight out of high school".

P19.note: Before/after contrast (papers ignored the club, later "one serious option") gives legitimized; "For a decade" kills launched.

P20.note: Naive over lenient rests on smugglers having to mislabel crates (deception was needed) plus "took each captain's word"; lenient remains defensible.

P21.note: "built barracks beside the town's station to house troops" gives garrison away; dormitory literally fits troops living there.

P22.note: "printed his on linen in sixteen panels hinged to fold flat" gives portable away.

P23.note: Repainting and feast-day lamps plus locked doors with no use; "doors stayed locked" kills refuge and platform, repainting kills quarry.

P24.note: "went on leafing out and growing as before" kills defoliated, felled and dwarfed in one phrase; the crumbling cores give honeycombed.

P25.note: "the one title in town they could not acquire, and inside its walls the old price agreement ... still held" gives stronghold.

P26.note: "ramps at every door ... shelves stood open to anyone who walked in" gives accessible away.

P27.note: Church funerals to dance halls with the prayer replaced; "kept the hill singers' hard voices" kills sweetened, unearthed is a mild lure.

P28.note: Stop, list, seal, refuse weapons reads as checkpoint, but the neutral-trust setup (neither lord trusted the other) makes broker defensible.

P29.note: "none of the other clauses could be applied" gives keystone; loophole is a lure from the court striking it down.

P30.note: "set out, step by step, how to call a meeting" gives handbook; members writing corrections kills gospel.

P31.note: "read aloud ... every payment the council had made without a vote" plus members repaying gives watchdog; distractors are weak.

P32.note: "its books held the life of nearly every boat on that coast" gives memory; insurer is a lure from buyers checking a hull's history.

P33.note: Broken legs fell while scrum and crowds stayed; "towns and villages alike" kills urbanized and "remained the heart of every match" kills splintered/unbalanced.

P34.note: Costumes, loudspeaker narrator, weeks of rehearsal make it a staged show; moving the time for visitors keeps democratized partly alive.

P35.note: Group-by-group exemptions give porous, but obsolete fits "fewer than one household in five"; only "still owed the duty" and "partly cleared" keep the rule alive.

P36.note: "multiplying the valley's figures by each district's area" makes it a stand-in; prototype is the near miss.

P37.note: Must combine "covered all twelve" with "four of the springs ... those four alone"; "generally accepted" kills rehabilitated.

P38.note: "readers meet the sisters only as he describes them" plus the colouring of identical behaviour gives prism; "speaks fewer lines" sits oddly with a novel told entirely in his letters.

P39.note: "nearly every young herring caught past the quays hatched in those pools" gives seedbed; the hydrology terms are surface lures only.

P40.note: Weekly attacks on each merger plan, each withdrawn, city kept its council: rampart; rudder (steering civic opinion) is a near miss.
